key_insight: The apparent gap between discrete and continuous visual generation stems not from an inherent weakness of discrete tokenizers but from the number of bits (compression ratio) in the latent space — increasing codebook size lets discrete methods match continuous pipelines.
problem_solved: Addresses the belief that discrete tokenizers are intrinsically inferior to continuous latent methods in autoregressive image generation by isolating the true cause of the performance gap.
method: Introduce Masked Bit Modeling within an autoregressive framework to operate on discrete latent codes.
Systematically vary the total number of bits (via codebook size) to study how compression ratio affects fidelity and generation quality.
Compare discrete and continuous pipelines under matched bit budgets to demonstrate that scaling codebook size closes the performance gap.
impact: Shows practitioners that choosing or designing discrete tokenizers should focus on available bit budget rather than assuming an inherent disadvantage—enabling discrete, scalable autoregressive models that can rival continuous approaches.
visual_elements: Line/bar chart: generation quality (e.g., FID/accuracy proxy) vs. total bits/codebook size showing convergence of discrete and continuous methods as bits increase.
Schematic: side-by-side pipeline diagrams of discrete (tokenizer + codebook) and continuous latent workflows with an annotation of bit budget.
Illustration: masked bit modeling mechanism (masking bits in discrete codes and autoregressive prediction) to convey the core modeling idea.
Icon set: codebook size, compression ratio (bits per pixel), and performance to summarize trade-offs visually.
paper_title: Autoregressive Image Generation with Masked Bit Modeling
paper_authors: Qihang Yu, Qihao Liu, Ju He, Xinyang Zhang, Yang Liu
